## Hypothesis tests

| # | Hypothesis | Evidence | p (Holm) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H4 | Meningioma is detected less reliably than the other classes | sensitivity difference -17.6% (CI -25.4% to -10.8%) | 0.002 | supported |
| H1 | Image-level CV overstates accuracy versus patient-level CV (leakage) | balanced accuracy 91.6% (effnet_image) vs 86.5% (EfficientNetB0); McNemar 201/49 discordant | 2.9e-22 | supported |
| H2 | Transfer learning (EfficientNetB0) beats the baseline CNN | balanced accuracy 87.2% (cnn_patient) vs 86.5% (EfficientNetB0); McNemar 171/173 discordant | 1 | not supported |
| H3 | Class weighting improves balanced accuracy | balanced accuracy 87.6% (effnet_patient_cw) vs 86.5% (EfficientNetB0); McNemar 73/55 discordant | 0.4 | not supported |
| H5a | Kaggle accuracy is higher when the image has a near-copy in Training | 99.3% vs 93.7% | 2.7e-08 | supported |
| H5b | Kaggle accuracy is higher when the image's patient is in Training | 97.7% vs 96.6% | 1 | not supported |
| H6 | SHAP attribution concentrates on the tumour more than chance | median 4.6% inside vs 1.2% area | 1.7e-25 | supported |

### Second training run of the selected backbone (the final model)

The final model is ResNet50 retrained on the same folds with its fold models saved. Only training randomness differs (GPU non-determinism, augmentation, dropout), so the gap between the two runs shows how much a single run can move.

- Balanced accuracy: screen run 90.7%, final run 90.1% (difference -0.6%, 95% CI -2.0% to +0.8%; McNemar p = 0.3).
- The two runs give the same predicted class for 93.8% of images.
- The final model was selected on these folds, so its estimate is somewhat optimistic; an external test set is needed to remove that bias.

## Do the explanations point at the tumour? (ResNet50)

150 held-out images (114 patients), each explained by the fold model that never saw the patient, scored against the radiologist's tumour mask.

| | SHAP (expected gradients) | Grad-CAM |
|---|---|---|
| Median share of positive attribution inside the tumour | 4.6% | 4.5% |
| Median tumour area (chance level) | 1.2% | 1.2% |
| Median ratio to chance | 3.6× | 3.7× |
| Wilcoxon p (above chance) | 2.4e-26 | 3e-25 |
| Pointing game: peak inside tumour | 42.0% (chance 2.2%) | 28.7% (chance 2.2%) |
| Energy in tumour, correct vs wrong predictions | 4.6% vs 4.7% | 4.5% vs 4.5% |

Sanity check (randomly initialised model): rank similarity of maps trained vs random — SHAP 0.53, Grad-CAM -0.06 (low = the maps depend on what the model learned). Energy in tumour: trained 11.7% vs random 2.1%.
- SHAP: **does not pass** (similarity ≥ 0.5): the maps mostly reflect image structure, not what the model learned, so they should not be read as the model's reasoning.
- Grad-CAM: **passes** (maps change when the learned weights are removed).
SHAP completeness (sum of attributions vs model output change): r = 0.89.

Compared with the pre-specified EfficientNetB0 (same procedure, its own 150 images):

| | ResNet50 SHAP | EfficientNetB0 SHAP | ResNet50 Grad-CAM | EfficientNetB0 Grad-CAM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Median energy inside tumour | 4.6% | 3.5% | 4.5% | 2.5% |
| Pointing game hit rate | 42.0% | 32.7% | 28.7% | 20.0% |
| Similarity to a random model (sanity; low = good) | 0.53 | 0.77 | -0.06 | 0.16 |
